name: mainstream_persistence
evidence: Murphy (1999) reports recent parent-child fertility correlations mostly 0.15-0.20; Murphy (2013), 46 populations in 28 countries, reports regional means from 0.09 to 0.19 in Europe and Northern America (DOI 10.1080/19485565.2013.833779).
provenance: Checked 2026-08-13 against the published Murphy (1999) text and the open-access Murphy (2013) paper; see docs/mechanism-parameter-audit.md.
notes: The 0.15 centre is directly supported. The wider 0.05-0.30 interval is deliberately conservative across settings. This is combined genetic plus cultural persistence, not heritability.

name: mainstream_propensity_cv
evidence: Published parity distributions confirm substantial completed-family-size dispersion, but the cited recollection did not identify a reproducible cohort microdistribution from which mean, variance and this CV can be computed.
provenance: Audited 2026-08-13 and left unverified. Derive from Human Fertility Database or comparable cohort-parity data before publication; see docs/mechanism-parameter-audit.md.
notes: Highest-leverage unresolved sourced row. It sets how far apart the latent low, middle and high propensity types are.

name: mainstream_types
evidence: None. A structural choice, not an estimate.
notes: Three latent fertility-propensity types with no ethnic, religious or political label attached.

name: group_retention_haredi
evidence: Israel Democracy Institute (Regev and Gordon 2020) estimates 13.3% of people aged 20-64 raised Haredi had left: 86.7% implied retention. Leaving differs sharply by faction (5.4% Hasidic, 8.6% Lithuanian, 26.4% Sephardi).
provenance: Checked 2026-08-13 against the IDI study summary and its CBS-based estimates; see docs/mechanism-parameter-audit.md.
notes: Definition is current Haredi identification, not religious belief or school enrollment. The interval reflects documented faction heterogeneity.

name: group_fertility_haredi
evidence: Israel CBS reports Haredi TFR 6.38 for 2020-2022; IDI's 2024 statistical report rounds this to 6.4 and documents a fall from 7.5 in 2003-2005.
provenance: Checked 2026-08-13 against Israel CBS Births and Fertility 2022 and IDI Annual Statistical Report on Haredi Society 2024; see docs/mechanism-parameter-audit.md.
notes: Period TFR is used only to initialize a named-group propensity relative to Israel's 2024 fertility, not as a model scoring target.

name: group_share_haredi
evidence: IDI's 2024 statistical report estimates 1,392,000 Haredim, 13.9% of Israel's 2024 population.
provenance: Checked 2026-08-13 against IDI Annual Statistical Report on Haredi Society 2024, which reports CBS-based population estimates; see docs/mechanism-parameter-audit.md.
notes: Applied to Israel only. The value is aligned to the model's 2024 fork year.

name: group_retention_amish
evidence: Anderson and Thiehoff (2025) analyze 117,259 coded individuals and estimate 84.46% retention at ages 40+, the best approximation to lifetime retention (DOI 10.1080/00324728.2025.2592576).
provenance: Checked 2026-08-13 against the open-access Population Studies paper; see docs/mechanism-parameter-audit.md.
notes: Retention varies by affiliation and cohort. The population-wide age-40+ estimate replaces a rounded recollection.

name: group_fertility_amish
evidence: Anderson and Thiehoff (2025) estimate an Amish TFR of 6.1 from 77,073 births in the 2002-2011 snapshot; earlier Holmes County work reported completed fertility of 6.33 among married women.
provenance: Checked 2026-08-13 against the open-access Population Studies paper (DOI 10.1080/00324728.2025.2592576); see docs/mechanism-parameter-audit.md.
notes: The directly measured TFR matches the quantity used to initialize the named-group propensity.

name: group_share_amish
evidence: The Young Center estimates 394,720 Amish residents in the United States in 2024, about 0.115% of a roughly 344 million U.S. population.
provenance: Checked 2026-08-13 against Young Center, Amish Population 2024; see docs/mechanism-parameter-audit.md.
notes: Applied to the United States only. Young Center counts horse-and-buggy Amish groups and excludes Beachy Amish and Amish Mennonites.

name: defector_high_propensity_weight
provenance: Scenario knob. Spec 6.5 argues defectors should keep part of the fertility profile for a generation or two; how much is not established.
notes: Share of children leaving a named group who land in the mainstream HIGH propensity type rather than being spread across the mainstream distribution.

name: development_decline_per_decade
evidence: None. This is the quantity the project is trying to learn, not one it can look up.
provenance: Scenario knob, and the most important one in the model. Spec 6.9 requires it be a stated path rather than a fitted trend.
notes: How much the fertility ENVIRONMENT falls per decade under continued development pressure: what a person of fixed propensity has, not what the population has.

name: development_floor
notes: Floor on the environment multiplier relative to 2024, so continued development pressure cannot drive the environment to zero.

name: group_convergence_per_generation
evidence: Group fertility differentials have narrowed in several documented cases, but no general rate is established.
provenance: Scenario knob. Spec 6.7 forbids extrapolating a small group's present behaviour unchanged after it becomes a large share of society.
notes: How much a named group's fertility advantage decays per generation under the convergence scenario.
